message.content: {"caption":"Two side-by-side system-instruction templates for extracting reusable memory items from successful and failed web-navigation trajectories.","description":"A paired text-panel diagram has two columns, each with a gray “System Instruction” header and a gray “Input Prompt” bar near the bottom. The left panel concerns success: it asks an expert in web navigation to use a user query and the corresponding trajectory to summarize useful insights based on the agent’s successful trajectory. The phrase “successfully accomplished the task” and the instruction to think why the trajectory is successful are highlighted in green. It says the memories should help with similar future tasks, allows at most three memory items, prohibits repeating similar or overlapping items, and says not to mention specific websites, queries, or string contents but to focus on generalizable insights. The right panel concerns failure: it asks for useful insights based on the agent’s failed trajectory. The phrase “attempted to resolve the task but failed” and the instruction to reflect on why the trajectory failed are highlighted in red. It likewise calls for generalizable memories, at most three items, no repetition or overlap, and no specific websites, queries, or string contents; it additionally asks for lessons or strategies to prevent future failure. Both panels specify a Markdown output template with “# Memory Item i,” a title, a one-sentence description, and one to three sentences of content about insights. Under each input-prompt bar are the labels “Query: <user query>” and “Trajectory: <trajectory that completes the query>.” No arrows or chart data are present.","figure_type":"diagram","chart_values":[]}
